Use reuse, optimal substructure, local decisions, and competitive strategies.

This family contains **6 independently navigable LeetCode topics**. Each topic has its own directory and a starting mathematical abstraction. The grouping is a learning aid, not part of LeetCode's official hierarchy.

## Topics

1. **[Dynamic Programming](../dynamic-programming/index.qmd)** — Reuse results of overlapping subproblems according to a recurrence.
2. **[Memoization](../memoization/index.qmd)** — Cache the outcome of repeated function calls on the same state.
3. **[Greedy](../greedy/index.qmd)** — Commit to locally attractive choices when an exchange proof supports global optimality.
4. **[Game Theory](../game-theory/index.qmd)** — Model strategic choices made by competing agents.
5. **[Minimax](../minimax/index.qmd)** — Optimise against an opponent's most damaging response.
6. **[Bitmask](../bitmask/index.qmd)** — Encode subsets compactly in the bits of an integer.

## Mathematical connection

A problem can carry several topic labels. Let $\mathcal Q$ be the **set of problems** and $\mathcal T$ the set of topic tags. The assignment of tags to problems is a set-valued mapping:

$$
L:\mathcal Q\longrightarrow\mathcal P(\mathcal T).
$$

Here $L(p)$ is the set of tags assigned to problem $p$. Tags describe relevant structures and techniques; they do **not** uniquely determine an algorithm or a proof of correctness.
